The '''United States Medical Center for Federal Prisoners''' ('''MCFP Springfield''') is a United States [[federal prison]] in [[Springfield, Missouri]], for male offenders. It is operated by the [[Federal Bureau of Prisons]], a division of the [[United States Department of Justice]].<ref>{{cite web|title=MCFP Springfield|url=http://www.bop.gov/locations/institutions/spg/index.jsp|publisher=Federal Bureau of Prisons|access-date=3 November 2013|archive-date=2013-11-02 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131102040600/http://www.bop.gov/locations/institutions/spg/index.jsp|url-status=live}}</ref>

==History==
During the [[Great Depression]], the city of Springfield, Missouri, offered {{convert|620|acre}} of land to the federal government to build the prison, under the direction of business leaser and Chamber of Commerce president [[John T. Woodruff]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=McConnell |first1=Kaitlyn |title=The Influential Dedication of John T. Woodruff |url=https://www.springfieldchamber.com/the-influential-dedication-of-john-t-woodruff/ |website=Springfield Area Chamber of Commerce |publisher=Springfield Area Chamber of Commerce |access-date=14 August 2025}}</ref> Congress authorized the building of the prison in 1930. The prison opened in 1933 as the "United States Hospital for [[defective delinquents|Defective Delinquents]]", under superintendent Marion R. King.<ref name="thelibraryorg">{{cite web|title=United States Medical Center for Federal Prisoners|url=http://thelibrary.org/lochist/postcards/medical_center_2.cfm|publisher=Springfield Greene County Library|access-date=June 24, 2012|archive-date=2012-10-18 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121018032958/http://thelibrary.org/lochist/postcards/medical_center_2.cfm|url-status=live}}</ref> The land surrounding the prison was used by the prisoners for farming until 1966. In 1977, the federal government returned some of the original 620 acres to the city.<ref name="thelibraryorg" /> [[Prison riots]] occurred in 1941, 1944 and 1959.<ref name="thelibraryorg" />

Several political prisoners and spies arrested during [[World War II]] were held at MCFP Springfield for medical treatment. [[Anastasy Vonsyatsky]] served 3 years of a 5-year sentence there for conspiring to aid Hitler's Germany in violation of the [[Espionage Act]] before being released in 1946.<ref>{{cite web|title=Anastase Vonsiatsky and Marion Ream papers|url=https://library.brown.edu/riamco/render.php?eadid=US-RPPC-vonsiatskyandream&view=biography|publisher=National Endowment for the Humanities|access-date=3 November 2013|archive-date=2013-11-04 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131104010420/http://library.brown.edu/riamco/render.php?eadid=US-RPPC-vonsiatskyandream&view=biography|url-status=live}}</ref> [[Robert Henry Best]] and [[Herbert John Burgman]], who were sentenced to life in prison for [[treason]] in 1948 and 1949 for making [[propaganda]] broadcasts for the [[Nazis]], served their sentences at this prison. Best died at MCFP Springfield in 1952, Burgman in 1953.<ref>{{cite news|last=Stadler|first=Glen|title=Portrait of a Traitor|url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=nYkRAAAAIBAJ&sjid=xeIDAAAAIBAJ&pg=5207,4366226&dq=robert-henry-best&hl=en|access-date=3 January 2013|newspaper=Eugene Register-Guard|date=Dec 27, 1952|archive-date=2020-05-19 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200519051655/https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=nYkRAAAAIBAJ&sjid=xeIDAAAAIBAJ&pg=5207%2C4366226&dq=robert-henry-best&hl=en|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|agency=Associated Press|title=Traitor Given Six to 20 Years|url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=qZAuAAAAIBAJ&sjid=ipkFAAAAIBAJ&pg=4521,4279675&dq=burgman+gestapo&hl=en|access-date=3 January 2013|newspaper=Montreal Gazette|date=Dec 21, 1949|archive-date=2022-02-25 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220225065022/https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=qZAuAAAAIBAJ&sjid=ipkFAAAAIBAJ&pg=4521%2C4279675&dq=burgman+gestapo&hl=en|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Standard Certificate of Death – Herbert John Burgman|url=http://www.sos.mo.gov/images/archives/deathcerts/1953/1953_00042600.PDF?debugMode=false&numberMarked=0|publisher=The Division of Health of Missouri|access-date=3 November 2013|date=December 28, 1953|archive-date=2012-10-05 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121005120446/http://www.sos.mo.gov/images/archives/deathcerts/1953/1953_00042600.PDF?debugMode=false&numberMarked=0|url-status=live}}</ref>

Several high-profile [[American Mafia|Mafia]] [[Boss (crime)|bosses]] received medical treatment at MCFP Springfield, including [[Joseph Bonanno]] of the [[Bonanno crime family]], [[Vito Genovese]] and [[Vincent Gigante]] of the [[Genovese crime family]] and [[John Gotti]] of the [[Gambino crime family]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Raab|first=Selwyn|title=John Gotti Dies in Prison at 61; Mafia Boss Relished the Spotlight|newspaper=The New York Times|date=June 11, 2002|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2002/06/11/nyregion/john-gotti-dies-in-prison-at-61-mafia-boss-relished-the-spotlight.html?pagewanted=all&src=pm|access-date=3 November 2013|archive-date=2016-12-23 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161223134516/http://www.nytimes.com/2002/06/11/nyregion/john-gotti-dies-in-prison-at-61-mafia-boss-relished-the-spotlight.html?pagewanted=all&src=pm|url-status=live}}</ref> Genovese died at MCFP Springfield in 1969, Gotti in 2002, and Gigante in 2005. Other notable inmates held at MCFP Springfield for treatment include [[Robert Stroud]], known as the "Birdman of Alcatraz" who died there in 1963, racecar driver [[Randy Lanier]], drug trafficker [[Michael Riconosciuto]], and "The Toxic Pharmacist" [[Robert Courtney (fraudster)|Robert Courtney]].<ref name="ST-19920119-guilty">{{cite news|url=https://archive.seattletimes.com/archive/19920119/1471110/jury-says-guilty|title=Jury Says Guilty -- Man Claims Frame-Up But Faces 20-Year Term After Verdict On Seven Drug-Related Charges|date=January 19, 1992|access-date=September 2, 2008|work=The Seattle Times|archive-date=2012-06-12 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120612013320/http://community.seattletimes.nwsource.com/archive/?date=19920119&slug=1471110|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|date=February 18, 2008 |url=http://www.newsmakingnews.com/vm,phillip,arthur,thompson,michael,riconosciuto,pull,strings,betty,cloer,murder,trial,2,18,08.htm |title=Is puppet master Michael Riconosciuto pulling the strings in the Betty Cloer murder trial?|author=Virginia Lee McCullough|access-date=August 17, 2010|publisher=NewsMakingNews |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101009164717/http://newsmakingnews.com/vm,phillip,arthur,thompson,michael,riconosciuto,pull,strings,betty,cloer,murder,trial,2,18,08.htm|archive-date=October 9, 2010|url-status=dead}}</ref> Terrorists [[Omar Abdel Rahman]] and [[José Padilla (criminal)|José Padilla]] were also held there for brief periods.

==Notable incidents==
On January 26, 2010, inmate Victor Castro-Rodriguez, 51, was found dead on the floor of his cell. Castro-Rodriguez originally was convicted of assault and resisting arrest in the U.S. District Court of Southern Florida and was being held at the MCFP because of a mental illness. MCFP inmates Wesley Paul Coonce Jr., 34, and Charles Michael Hall, 43, were charged in connection with his death and on May 7, 2014, were convicted of one count of first-degree murder. Coonce was also found guilty of one count of murder by an inmate serving a life sentence. Both were sentenced to death on June 2, 2014.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.news-leader.com/story/news/crime/2014/06/03/two-fed-med-inmates-sentenced-death-killing/9905907/|title=Two Fed Med inmates sentenced to death in killing|author=News-Leader Staff|date=3 June 2014|work=Springfield News-Leader|access-date=1 May 2015|archive-date=2018-01-28 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180128210315/http://www.news-leader.com/story/news/crime/2014/06/03/two-fed-med-inmates-sentenced-death-killing/9905907/|url-status=live}}</ref>

| John "The Teflon Don" Gotti was head of New York's [[Gambino crime family]]. One of the most powerful and dangerous crime bosses in the world, Gotti was charged with five counts of murder, conspiracy to commit murder, loansharking, illegal gambling, obstruction of justice, bribery and tax evasion. Convicted on all counts, he was sentenced to life imprisonment without possibility of parole and a $250,000 fine.

==In popular culture==
[[Johnny Sacrimoni|John Sacrimoni]], [[crime boss|boss]] of the fictional [[Lupertazzi crime family]] in the hit [[HBO]] television series ''[[The Sopranos]]'', dies at MCFP Springfield in the season 6 episode entitled "[[Stage 5 (The Sopranos episode)|Stage 5]]".

Ercole "Eckley" DiMeo of the fictional [[Soprano family|Soprano crime family]] in the hit [[HBO]] television series ''[[The Sopranos]]'' is only seen in the many Saints of Newark and is the boss of the [[DiMeo crime family]] and it is mentioned in season one that he is incarcerated here.

The American crime drama hit limited series ''[[Black Bird (miniseries)|Black Bird]]'' follows the true story of FBI Operative [[Jimmy Keene]] (birth name James Keene) during his time at MCFP Springfield. The series is based on the 2010 autobiographical novel ''In with the Devil: a Fallen Hero, a Serial Killer, and a Dangerous Bargain for Redemption'' by James Keene with Hillel Levin.
